newsitem.title: LATVIA: REVIEW-MARKETS FOCUS ON RESULTS IN MIXED WEEK OF TRADE.
newsitem.headline: REVIEW-MARKETS FOCUS ON RESULTS IN MIXED WEEK OF TRADE.

text.p: Baltic markets were focused on results this week, with Estonia's moving in response to the first batch of June banking figures and Lithuania and Latvia's bourses still waiting, dealers and analysts said on Friday.
Steady gains were expected in Estonia as more results come in but the outlook for Latvia and Lithuania was cloudy.
All three countries remain largely divorced from trends outside the region and tend to respond to domestic stimuli.
Dealers and analysts welcomed an initiative by the Latvian and Estonian securities commissions to lay the groundwork for an eventual merger of Baltic stock markets.
Dealers said one regional market would attract move foreign investment than the three small bourses combined and stregthen the partners' competitiveness against other emerging markets.
But talks are only in their infant stage and a blue-print for a pan-Baltic bourse is a long way off.
ESTONIA
Estonia's liquid bourse caught its breath after surging last week but picked up steam on Thursday as the first June banking results hit the market.
The Talse index closed at 279.03 on Thursday, up from 277.93 the previous Thursday.
Hoiupank's release of its June figures on Thursday, which showed a record 18.8 million kroon profit, drove its price up 2.5 kroons to 154 kroons.

Tallinna Pank's June profit of 4.4 million kroons fell short of the market's expectations, but its price was buoyed on Thursday by an announcement that it planned to acquire a 100 percent stake in Saules Bank in neighbouring Latvia.
LATVIA
The Latvian stock exchange's recently introduced index rose to 384.92 on Thursday from 382.96 the week before but a listless market amid high summer temperatures kept turnover low.
Investors are seen favouring privatisation vouchers over equities ahead of the sell-off of several key assets.
Dealers welcomed the news that insurer Balta, the biggest insurance company in the Baltics, planned to go public and hoped to be listed on the bourse in autumn.
The struggling market is badly in need of a fresh batch of bigger and more liquid companies like Balta to inject new life into it.
In the short-term, activity is not seen significantly increasing until a spate of six-month results for key companies come out.
But dealers are divided over what impact the results will have on prices.
LITHUANIA
Lithuania's indices over the week showed a mixed performance and turnover was generally slow.

The official index, which tracks the five top blue chips, slipped to 882.03 points on Thursday from 884.41 the previous week, while the wider group A index inched up to 1874.16 points from 1871.71 points in the same period.
Central market activity was sluggish most of the week as the seasonal summer bearishness set in and the market nervously waits for six-month results.
Oil terminal Klaipedos Nafta gave the bourse a bit of a boost, with over eight percent of its shares swapping hands in block trades worth over seven million litas in the last few days.
Brokers said a foreign investor was involved but would not say who.
